claim: A pull request carrying a failing test is mechanically prevented from merging into the protected main branch. Not declined by a reviewer, and not merely configured as required: refused by GitHub, naming the failing check.

disposable_pull_request.why_pytest_fail_not_assert_false: flake8-bugbear B011 rejects `assert False`, so the branch would have failed at the linter. The file is deliberately ruff-clean and mypy --strict clean so that every gate before the test run lets it through and the thing which rejects it is the test result.

merge_attempts.message: Merge commits are not allowed on this repository.
New changes require approval from someone other than the last pusher. Required status check "required" is failing.

known_limits: The first squash attempt, made before the eight core jobs had re-reported, was refused with 'Required status check "required" is expected' rather than 'is failing'. Both refusals are recorded because the distinction matters: a check that has not reported blocks a merge for a different reason than a check that failed, and T3.3 is about the second.

prevent_self_review is false and the repository has one collaborator, so the approving-review requirement cannot be satisfied by anyone at present. That is a property of the repository, not of this proof: the refusal names the failing status check independently.

The release-candidate environment's deployment_branch_policy had to be removed for this proof to run at all; see the U1 runbook. Its protected_branches_only value was incompatible with a gate that triggers on pull_request.
